title: Man. Post. Cap. VII: PLAC Adam's goods inseparable from faithfulness
pass_a_gloss: Adam's sin—the condition's breach—was unfaithfulness, disobedience, pride, aversion from God, conversion to creatures, and the rest, which cannot stand with perfect rectitude, justice, holiness, innocence. Another difference: to strip the courtier of royal gifts after broken faith needs the King's or a judge's act—judgment and execution—or else he keeps titles, dignities, and estates.
pass_b_english: But what was the violation of the condition—Adam's sin? unfaithfulness, disobedience, ambition, pride, ingratitude, greed, curiosity, aversion from God, conversion to creatures, &c.—which, how they could have stood with perfect rectitude, justice, holiness, innocence, I for my part cannot understand. Hence another difference is born: for faith being violated, that the Courtier be deprived of the goods received from the King, there is need of the King's or a judge's action, namely judgment and execution of judgment. Otherwise those titles, dignities, and estates would be retained by the Courtier.
source_text: Quaenam autem fuit conditionis violatio, quod peccatum Adami? infidelitas, inobedientia, ambitio, superbia, ingratitudo, cupedia, curiositas, a Deo aversio, ad creaturas conversio &c. quae, quomodo cum perfecta rectitudine, justitia, sanctitate, innocentia consistere potuerint, equidem intelligere non possum. Hinc aliud nascitur discrimen, nam violata fide, ut bonis a Rege acceptis Aulicus privetur, opus est Regis, vel judicis actione, nempe judicio, & judicii executione. Alioqui tituli illi, dignitates, & fundi retinerentur ab Aulico.
